verses.1: A burden of the word of the LORD to Israel by my hand.
verses.2: I have loved you, says the LORD. And you ask, How have you loved us? Was not Esau a brother to Jacob? says the LORD. I have loved Jacob.
verses.3: But I have hated Esau, and I have laid his mountains in desolation, and his inheritance into a wasteland of the desert.
verses.4: Because Edom says, We are shattered, and we will return, and we will build the ruins. Thus says the LORD of Hosts: They will build, and I will tear down. And they will be called the boundary of wickedness. And the people who have been angry the LORD has held to the end.
verses.5: And your eyes will see, and you will say, The LORD has been exalted beyond the boundary of Israel.
verses.6: A son honors a father, and a servant his master. If I am a father, where is my glory? If I am a master, where is my fear? says the LORD of Hosts. To you, the priests who despise my name, you ask, In what way have we despised your name?
verses.7: You bring defiled food on my altar. And you say, In what way have we defiled you? Because you say, The table of the LORD is defiled.
verses.8: But if you bring a blind animal to be sacrificed, is that not evil? And if you bring a lame or a sick one, is that not evil? Bring it to your ruler, will he please you, will he accept your face? says the LORD of Hosts.
verses.9: And now, indeed, seek the face of God, that He may have mercy on you. But from your hands this has come. Will He accept your face? says the LORD of Hosts.
verses.10: For even among you the doors will be shut, and my altar will not be kindled in vain. I have no pleasure in you, says the LORD of Hosts. And I will not accept a sacrifice from your hands.
verses.11: For from the rising of the sun to its setting, great is my name among the nations, and in every place incense is brought to my name, and a pure offering, because great is my name among the nations, says the LORD of Hosts.
verses.12: But you profane it, by saying, The table of the Lord is defiled, and the offering that is laid there is despised.
verses.13: You say, Behold, a burden! And you weary it. You bring what is taken by force, and the lame and the sick, and you bring the offering. Will I accept this from your hands? says the LORD.
verses.14: Cursed is the one who swears falsely, and there is a male in his flock, and he vows and sacrifices a defective one to the Lord. For I am a great king, says the LORD of Hosts, and my name is feared among the nations.

notes:
Notes
- v. 11: "the nations" (הַגּוֹיִם) is used in contrast to Israel, emphasizing the universal reverence for the LORD's name.
- v. 13: "a burden" (מַתְּלָאָה) likely refers to the sacrificial offering, which the people treat with weariness and disregard.
